summary: Aathman backend fully tested via public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. 28/28 pytest cases pass covering: health, OTP send/verify (dev mode), auth middleware (401 without/invalid token), profile update, meditations list+filter, meditation session logging → stats/streak update, mantra jaap counter, mood check-in + weekly stats, diary CRUD, national rank leaderboard including self, live sessions (satsang/yoga), books list+detail+404, order create with mock_mode=true and MOCKED razorpay verify → paid, guru messages/quote, Q&A create+seeded answers, SOS request, sleep music. Previous-OTP invalidation and wrong-OTP 400 also verified. Note: Razorpay verify and SendGrid are MOCKED as declared.

minor.issue: Returns dev_otp in response even in production when SENDGRID_API_KEY is empty (send fails ⇒ dev_otp exposed). Consider gating strictly on OTP_DEV_MODE for production.

For scope='international' code skips filtering (comment says 'all') but earlier 'national' filter still applies only when both users have nationality; users with null nationality would leak into national scope. Minor edge case.
Uses body.dict() (Pydantic v1 API). If Pydantic v2 is installed, this emits a deprecation warning; prefer body.model_dump(exclude_none=True).

action_items: Optional: harden dev_otp exposure so it is only ever returned when OTP_DEV_MODE=true (not when SendGrid send fails silently).
Optional: migrate body.dict() → body.model_dump() for Pydantic v2 forward-compat.

Frontend .env exposes EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (correct for Expo). System prompt references EXPO_BACKEND_URL – tests fall back to EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL, which is what Expo web actually uses. No action needed unless main agent wants both keys.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py (~860 lines) is close to the 700-line guideline threshold; consider splitting routers (auth, content, commerce, guru) into modules as the app grows.
Rank endpoint: 'circle' scope currently returns only the requesting user – acceptable for MVP but should be documented.
Order.create stores amount in INR (rupees) while razorpay expects paise; fine for MOCK mode but ensure real integration multiplies by 100 (it does).
seed_data_creation: No manual seed – backend seeds meditations, sleep_content, live_sessions, books, guru_messages, quotes, Q&A on startup. Tests create per-test TEST_-prefixed users/diary/orders which are safe to leave.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend base URL comes from /app/frontend/.env → EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL). Use conftest fixture 'user_session' + 'auth_headers' for authenticated tests. Razorpay and SendGrid are MOCKED (no keys). To retest: `pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`.
mocked_apis_verified: Razorpay verify: /api/orders/create returns mock_mode=true, /api/orders/verify returns ok=true, status=paid without signature
SendGrid: /api/auth/send-otp returns dev_otp instead of sending email
